title: Pre-existing buyers - do they get any protection under the new housing law
p1:
Bought a home before the new housing law came into force? You may be wondering — do the new protections apply to you too?

Many buyers assume that new laws only help future customers. That is not always true.
p2: A common misunderstanding is that existing buyers automatically lose all protection. In reality, the answer often depends on when the agreement was signed, what stage the project was in, and whether the issue relates to ongoing obligations or past actions.
p3:
For example, a buyer who booked a property earlier may still have rights regarding delayed possession, promised facilities, or unfair practices if those matters fall within the law's scope. The date of purchase alone does not always decide everything.

The practical lesson: before accepting that a new law does not apply, check your agreement, project status, and the specific protection being claimed.
conclusion: Do you think buyers who booked homes before a new housing law should receive the same protections as new buyers? Share your view.
